newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico commercial feed output falls in '96 - ASA.
newsitem.headline: Mexico commercial feed output falls in '96 - ASA.

text.p: Total commercial feed output in Mexico dipped around 10.6 percent in 1996 over 1995 levels, the local office of the American Soybean Association (ASA) said Monday.

In an update, the ASA said commerical feed output, excluding feed production from integrated operators, dropped to 3.505 million tonnes last year from 3.921 million tonnes in 1995 and 4.421 tonnes in 1994.
Citing figures from the major feed manuafacturers' associations in Mexico, the ASA said 1994 figures were record levels for the country.

"The commericial feed industry continues to lose volume and market share to the integrated operations...best estimates of total feed production in Mexico are about 13.505 million tonnes for 1996," the ASA said.
"This means that integrated feed production is around 10 million tonnes. This also means that commerical feed is down to about 26 percent of total feed produced in Mexico," it added.
Integrated operations are those such as large poultry companies which produce their own feed.
But the ASA said there is probably more feed produced in Mexico than officially reported because production figures do not match total feed grain imports and local production.

"There are a large undetermined number of small feed mills or simply forage outlets and grain mixing stores around the country that do not report volumes to any association or to the government tax authorities," the ASA said.
It added this phenomenon could account for some of the disparity.
((--Chris Aspin, Mexico City newsroom (525) 7289530. E-mail at chris.aspin@reuters.com))
